newsitem.title: USA: Ashland to sell Blazer unit to Norway's Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Ashland to sell Blazer unit to Norway's Statoil.

text.p: Ashland Inc. said Wednesday it has a definitive agreement to sell its Blazer Energy Corp. subsidiary to Statoil of Norway for $566 million in cash.
The deal, which includes virtually all of Ashland's domestic oil and natural gas assets, will be made through Statoil's U.S. subidiary, the Eastern Group Inc.
The Ashland, Ky.-based oil and energy company said the deal is expected to close by July 1, subject to approval by regulators and Statoil's supervisory board.
Statoil said Blazer's Appalachian Basin properties will be retained by Eastern, while its Gulf of Mexico properties will be operated by Statoil Exploration (U.S.) Inc.

"This cash sale has potential to build shareholder value in several ways, including debt reduction and accelerated investment in our growth areas," said Paul Chellgren, chairman and chief executive of Ashland.
"We are also pleased that the Statoil affiliates have indicated that they hope to retain a large number of Blazer Energy employees."

Chellgren said Ashland plans to continue following its previously announced plan to boost profits by redirecting freed capital to growth businesses, including Ashland Chemical Co., the APAC highway construction group and Valvoline.
Ashland is engaged in petroleum refining and marketing, coal and highway construction.
Its stock rose $1 to $47 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
